title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas, while a human safety operator was present in the vehicle. The vehicle was in autonomous mode and did not slow down or stop for the animal. This represents a failure of the system to recognize and avoid a small, moving obstacle in an urban neighborhood setting.

The incident shows a gap between what the vehicle's sensors and planning systems detected and what action they took. The operator present did not intervene to prevent the collision. It is not established whether the system's perception failed to identify the duck, whether it identified but did not classify the duck as an obstacle requiring avoidance, or whether the safety operator could have reasonably intervened.

The company's subsequent analysis found the vehicle stopped appropriately at traffic control devices, and has responded by excluding certain streets from testing and planning technological improvements. Community concern about the incident was heightened because the duck was known to residents, though this does not bear on the technical failure.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, drawing significant community backlash. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, ran over the duck without stopping or slowing down. The duck had been nesting in a pot outside a local Italian restaurant, making it familiar to residents and intensifying their concerns about autonomous vehicle safety in their neighborhood.

In response to the outrage, Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode at the time of the incident. The company investigated the situation and reviewed vehicle data through multiple simulations, concluding the car did stop appropriately at all relevant stop signs, contradicting a resident's claim otherwise. Avride has excluded certain streets around the lake from its testing operations and is now evaluating technological improvements to prevent similar incidents. Meanwhile, local residents have preserved the duck's eggs in an incubator.
